More bitz, same ideas: 2026 Intercessor Squad, Outriders, Vanguard Veterans, Eradicators & Land Speeder unboxed

Stahly, September 19, 2026 1
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 11:40
Instaread

We’re at the start of a new Warhammer 40k edition, and one thing is as certain as death and taxes: a flood of new Space Marine kits. But how much of what’s in the new Intercessor Squad, the multipart Vanguard Veterans and Outriders, and the Eradicators and Land Speeder is actually new? We’ve unboxed every kit for you, with high-res sprue images, a walkthrough of the assembly instructions, and a full breakdown of every build option.

The new Space Marines codex and models will be available for pre-order starting Saturday, 26 September 2026. The pre-order period lasts two weeks, with the official release date set for 10 October 2026.

(Pre)order Space Marines

The Space Marines summer 2026 release wave review
This site contains affiliate links you can use to support Tale of Painters. As Amazon Associates, eBay partners, and partners of our partner shops we earn from qualifying purchases. Thanks :)

Part 1 of our big Space Marines review covers the new multipart Intercessor Squad, Outrider Squad, and Vanguard Veterans. We’ll also tell you whether the Eradicator Squad with Heavy Bolters and the Land Speeder box differ from the models in the Armageddon launch box or the starter sets. Part 2 follows next Tuesday, casting a light on the Captain on Bike and Kaius Konorius.

In this video, we unbox the entire release wave and flip through the assembly instructions, including the new Space Marines Captain on bike and Kaius Konorius:

Intercessor Squad reforged: up- or downgrade?

Nearly 9 years on, Games Workshop has finally given the Primaris Intercessor Squad kit a proper refresh. Beyond the cosmetic changes, the biggest shift is the sprue layout. The old kit had a two-part sprue with 5 poses/models, with two copies included per box. The new kit uses a three-part sprue with 10 models instead. So you get 10 different poses rather than 5, though net sprue count actually drops from 4 segments to 3. You also get 32mm bases, assembly instructions, and the familiar transfer sheet with Ultramarines, Imperial Fists, Salamanders, and Raptors iconography from recent editions.

Patreon bonus content: Ultra high-res, uncompressed versions of these sprue images (and backsides of the sprues) can be downloaded here.

Ad • Support our work through these partner links:

The build options:

  • 10 different bodies/poses

Interchangeable parts:

  • 10 different shin armour pairs
  • 10 power packs (in 5 different designs: 2x 118, 119, 3x 120, 2x 121, 122)
  • 6 bare heads (136 to 141)
  • 13 helmeted heads across 11 different designs (2x 124, 2x 125, 126 to 135), including 1 Mk6 helmet (131), 2 Mk7 helmets (132 and 133), 1 Mk8 helmet (135)
  • 8 arm pairs with bolt rifles, 1 arm pair (66 and 67) with bolt rifle (68) or bolt rifle with auxiliary grenade launcher (69), 1 arm pair with bolt rifle and aux. grenade launcher (99 and 100), 3 right arms with bolt rifles plus 1 left arm with knife, 1 pointing left arm, 1 left arm with auspex, 1 left arm with grenade
  • 20 plain shoulder pads, 1 Mk6 shoulder pad with rivets (111), 1 plain Mk6 shoulder pad (112)
  • 3 optional small icons, 1 measuring device, 1 book, 1 upper helmet piece (all for attaching to the belt), 5 purity seals
  • For the Sergeant: 2 right arms (raised 8, extended 9), 2 right hands with plasma pistol (10) or bolt pistol (11), 1 right arm with raised bolt rifle (101), 1 left arm with chainsword (12), 1 left arm with power sword (13), 1 left power fist (14), 1 bolt rifle for slinging over the shoulder (7), holstered bolt pistol (5) and empty holster (6), 1 Mk10 helmet with skull (123), 1 Mk7 helmet with skull (134), 2 shoulder pads with plaque (109 and 110), 2 different tilting shields (148 and 149), 1 power pack (113) with optional back banner (114), 2 different small icons (115 and 116), or a plain cover (117)

Fewer sprues, more variety

Down to 3 sprue segments instead of 4, is that shrinkflation? The kit definitely has to work with less plastic. That plastic is put to excellent use, though. Thanks to 10 poses instead of 5, more individually sculpted armour, and a wide selection of heads, the kit actually feels noticeably more varied despite the reduced sprue count. As before, the shoulder join points stay flat and universal, so heads and shoulder pads remain compatible with other Primaris kits.

What’s been cut are the auto bolt rifle and stalker bolt rifle parts. As the new datasheet already hinted, Intercessors now come with standard bolt rifles only, matching the monopose models from Armageddon and the 11th edition Warhammer 40k starter sets (our review with sprue images here). Plenty of pouches and knives are also sculpted directly onto the bodies now rather than being separate parts, which saves space. That said, the old Intercessor kit did have somewhat more individualised shoulder pads.

Multipart Outrider Squad review: real build options at last

The Outrider Squad originally launched in the Indomitus launch box and was also part of the 9th edition Warhammer 40,000 starter sets. The old kit was monopose, though, with no weapon options at all. That changes with the new kit.

The box contains 3 Outriders on a sprue with 3 segments, plus 90mm oval bases, assembly instructions, and a transfer sheet.

Patreon bonus content: Ultra high-res, uncompressed versions of these sprue images (and backsides of the sprues) can be downloaded here.

The build options:

  • All 3 bikes are identical. On each bike, you can glue the wheels into three different positions, keeping the bike upright or leaning it left or right.
  • 3 different riders (these are entirely separate from the bike and have flat shoulder connectors and ball joints for the heads, making them compatible with every other Primaris Space Marine kit).
  • 3 right and 3 left arms for the handlebars
  • 3 holstered bolt pistols and 3 empty holsters, which attach to the inside of the front fairing

Interchangeable parts:

  • 4 left forearms with chainswords in different poses
  • 6 left arms for melee weapons
  • 2 right arms with heavy bolt pistols, 1 right arm with plasma pistol
  • 7 bare heads, 1 with a half-mask (70)
  • 3 helmets
  • 3 right shoulder pads with extended trim, 3 plain shoulder pads, 1 shoulder pad with plaque
  • 3 power packs
  • 6 optional pouches and grenades for the belts
  • 2 optional sheathed chainswords, 3 empty sword sheaths for the bikes
  • For the Sergeant: 1 left forearm with power sword (22), 1 left forearm with power hammer (41), 1 left forearm with power axe (52), 1 helmet with skull symbol (66), 1 optional tilting shield (24)

Even though not much seems to have changed at first glance compared to the monopose Outriders, the kit actually offers plenty of options. Every model can either keep both hands on the handlebars or be armed with a melee weapon or a pistol. On top of that, you get 6 arm poses for melee weapons and special weapons for the Sergeant. For easier painting, rider and bike stay separate this time round. One problem from the old kit doesn’t get fixed in the new version, though: the bikes are still built from two halves, so a seam line runs right through the middle, particularly noticeable on the front fairing.

Multipart Vanguard Veterans unboxed: shield yourself

Alongside the Intercessors, the Vanguard Veterans from Armageddon and the starter sets also get a multipart kit with more weapon options. The box contains 5 models on a sprue with 3 medium-sized segments, 32mm bases, assembly instructions, and transfers.

The build options:

  • 5 different bodies/poses with jump packs
  • Each body comes with a matching belt piece, either with an empty holster (for the pistol arms) or with grenades and pouches (for the shield arms)
  • Veteran pose 1 builds as Sergeant or a regular Veteran. The Sergeant gets specially sculpted right leg armour (69), 1 right arm with power fist (82 and 83), 1 right arm with power hammer (80), and 1 right arm with master-crafted power sword (81). The arms have flat shoulder connectors and, in theory, fit other bodies too. This model also includes 2 ruin pieces for the right foot (71 or 72).
  • Veteran pose 2 chooses between 2 left leg armour pieces (20 and 21).
  • Veteran pose 3 chooses between 2 right leg armour pieces (37 and 38).
  • Veteran pose 4 chooses between 2 right leg armour pieces (53 and 54).
  • Veteran pose 5 chooses between 2 left leg armour pieces (5 and 6).

Patreon bonus content: Ultra high-res, uncompressed versions of these sprue images (and backsides of the sprues) can be downloaded here.

Interchangeable parts:

  • 10 helmeted heads, including 1 Mk6 (110), 2 Mk7 (104 and 108), 2 Mk8 (105 and 106)
  • 9 bare heads, 3 with half-masks (117 to 119)
  • 5 right shoulder pads with Crux Terminatus
  • 6 left shoulder pads with extended trim, 1 of these Mk6 with rivets (100)
  • 7 pouches and icons (120 to 126), 3 large purity seals (127 to 129), 1 tilting shield (130), 5 small purity seals (131 to 135)
  • 5 left arms with power swords (1 of these bionic, part 42), 3 left arms with power axes
  • 5 right arms with heavy bolt pistols, 3 right arms with plasma pistols
  • 5 right arms with combat shields, 1 right arm with a larger shield for the Sergeant (75 and 77)

This kit is also absolutely packed, with plenty of heads and bitz for your bits box. Thanks to the universal, flat join points on the arms, you can create a huge range of poses. You also get the choice of arming the whole unit with pistols or, new compared to the monopose Vanguard Veterans, with combat shields. Another difference: the monopose models leap from the jagged rock formations typical of Armageddon’s deserts, while the multipart Veterans are posed atop imperial architectural ruins instead. A nice touch is that empty holsters are included specifically for the pistol loadout. Raven Guard fans will likely be disappointed, though, that lightning claws are nowhere to be found.

Standalone Eradicators and Land Speeder release: anything new?

Unlike the Eradicators with melta rifles, which got their own dedicated multipart box, the Eradicator Squad with Heavy Bolters contains the same monopose models from the Armageddon launch box. There, they were part of a larger sprue; for this box, the models have simply been rearranged onto a smaller one. Otherwise, the sculpts are completely identical. As with Armageddon, the only build option is choosing between a helmet or bare head for the Sergeant.

The Land Speeder uses the identical sprue from Armageddon and the 40k starter sets. The only change is that the box now includes a transparent flight stand too, letting you skip the rock formation that otherwise holds the model in the air. The kit was always designed with this option in mind, though the transparent stand itself was left out of the Armageddon and 40k starter set releases. More about the Land Speeder kit (plus sprue pics) in our review of the starter sets.

8.5
Score

Pros

  • Intercessors pack 10 unique poses despite fewer sprue segments
  • Outriders and Vanguard Veterans offer more weapon options than their monopose predecessors
  • All heads, arms and shoulder pads stay compatible across Primaris kits

Cons

  • Intercessor auto and stalker bolt rifle options are gone for good
  • Outrider bikes still have a visible seam line down the middle
  • Eradicators are essentially unchanged rehashes from Armageddon
Intercessor Squad
9
Outrider Squad
8
Vanguard Veterans
9

Final Verdict

All three new multipart kits are stuffed with build options and extra bitz, and every model stays fully compatible with other Primaris Space Marines. So, well done, job done. But this wave of Space Marine releases doesn't really bring anything genuinely new to the table. Everything here has existed in some form before, whether as a monopose model or as part of the Firstborn range. The Astartes model range has become a bit more rounded and complete as a result, but it does make me wonder where this is all heading before GW runs into the Stormcast problem: a model range that keeps growing and growing until it eventually starts cannibalising itself. The first Primaris models have already been pulled from the range, after all.
